subject: Mathematics
subtopic: Arithmetic & Geometric Progressions, Partial Sums & Mathematical Induction
text: MoEYS Grade 11 Mathematics Chapter 1: Real Number Sequences, Arithmetic Progressions (ស្វ៊ីតនព្វន្ត), and Geometric Progressions (ស្វ៊ីតធរណីមាត្រ). An arithmetic progression (AP) has constant common difference d = u_{n+1} - u_n, general term u_n = u_1 + (n - 1)d, and sum of first n terms S_n = n(u_1 + u_n)/2. A geometric progression (GP) has constant common ratio q = u_{n+1}/u_n, general term u_n = u_1 q^{n-1}, and partial sum S_n = u_1(1 - q^n)/(1 - q) for q != 1 (with infinite sum S = u_1/(1 - q) when |q| < 1).

concepts.title: Arithmetic Progressions (ស្វ៊ីតនព្វន្ត)
concepts.summary: Constant difference d, general term u_n = u_1 + (n - 1)d, and sum S_n.
concepts.body: A sequence (u_n) is arithmetic if u_{n+1} - u_n = d (constant). Any term is u_n = u_k + (n - k)d, three consecutive terms a, b, c satisfy 2b = a + c, and the sum of n terms is S_n = n(u_1 + u_n)/2 = (n/2)[2u_1 + (n - 1)d].

concepts.title: Geometric Progressions (ស្វ៊ីតធរណីមាត្រ)
concepts.summary: Constant ratio q, general term u_n = u_1 q^{n-1}, and finite/infinite sums.
concepts.body: A sequence (u_n) is geometric if u_{n+1} = q u_n. The n-th term is u_n = u_1 q^{n-1}, three consecutive terms satisfy b^2 = ac, and for q != 1 the sum of n terms is S_n = u_1(q^n - 1)/(q - 1). If |q| < 1, lim_{n->inf} S_n = u_1 / (1 - q).

formulas.name: Geometric Progression (GP) General Term & Sum
formulas.expression: u_n = u_1 q^{n-1}, \quad S_n = u_1 \frac{q^n - 1}{q - 1} \; (q \neq 1), \quad S_\infty = \frac{u_1}{1 - q} \; (|q| < 1)

examples.problem: An arithmetic progression has first term u_1 = 3 and common difference d = 4. Find the 10th term u_{10} and the sum of the first 10 terms S_{10}.
A geometric progression has u_1 = 2 and common ratio q = 3. Find u_5 and S_5.

exercises.prompt: Find the infinite sum of the geometric series 8 + 4 + 2 + 1 + 1/2 + ...
hints: Identify u_1 = 8 and q = 1/2, then apply S = u_1 / (1 - q).

solution_steps: Step 1: Test whether u_{n+1} - u_n is constant (AP) or u_{n+1}/u_n is constant (GP).
Step 2: Identify u_1, d (or q), and term count n.
Step 3: Substitute into the general term and sum formulas.

common_misconceptions.text: Using exponent n instead of (n - 1) in the n-th term of a GP (writing u_n = u_1 q^n).
common_misconceptions.correction: When starting at index 1 (u_1), the n-th term has (n - 1) steps, so u_n = u_1 q^{n-1}.

common_misconceptions.text: Miscounting the number of terms from u_k to u_n as (n - k) instead of (n - k + 1).
common_misconceptions.correction: From index k to index n inclusive, there are (n - k + 1) terms.

subject: Mathematics
subtopic: Exponent & Logarithm Laws, Change of Base, Equations & Inequalities
text: MoEYS Grade 11 Mathematics Chapter 2: Exponential and Logarithmic Functions (អនុគមន៍និទស្សន្ត និងអនុគមន៍លោការីត). For base a > 0, a != 1, y = a^x is defined on R with range (0, +inf), and its inverse is the base-a logarithm y = log_a(x) defined for x > 0: log_a(x) = y <=> a^y = x. Logarithm rules transform products into sums, quotients into differences, and powers into multiples. When solving logarithmic or exponential inequalities, monotonicity depends on the base: strictly increasing if a > 1 (inequality direction preserved) and strictly decreasing if 0 < a < 1 (inequality direction reversed).

metadata.topic_khmer: អនុគមន៍និទស្សន្ត និងអនុគមន៍លោការីត

learning_objectives: Apply algebraic rules of rational exponents and logarithms (product, quotient, power, and change-of-base rules)
Solve exponential equations a^{f(x)} = a^{g(x)} and quadratic-in-a^x equations
Solve logarithmic equations and inequalities by enforcing the domain condition u(x) > 0 and checking whether base a > 1 or 0 < a < 1

concepts.title: Properties of Exponents & Logarithms (លក្ខណៈស្វ័យគុណ និងលោការីត)
concepts.summary: Definition log_a(b) = c <=> a^c = b and algebraic identities.
concepts.body: For a > 0, a != 1 and M, N > 0: log_a(1) = 0, log_a(a) = 1, a^{log_a M} = M, log_a(MN) = log_a M + log_a N, log_a(M/N) = log_a M - log_a N, log_a(M^k) = k log_a M, and change of base log_a(b) = ln(b)/ln(a).

concepts.title: Exponential & Logarithmic Equations and Inequalities (សមីការ និងវិសមភាព)
concepts.summary: Domain restrictions M > 0 and base comparison a > 1 vs 0 < a < 1.
concepts.body: Before combining logarithms in an equation or inequality, always state the domain where every logarithm argument is strictly positive (> 0). For inequalities log_a f(x) < log_a g(x): if a > 1, 0 < f(x) < g(x); if 0 < a < 1, f(x) > g(x) > 0.

khmer_terms.Exponential and Logarithmic Functions: អនុគមន៍និទស្សន្ត និងអនុគមន៍លោការីត

khmer_terms.natural logarithm: លោការីតនេពែរ (ln)

formulas.name: Logarithm Laws & Change of Base Formula
formulas.expression: \log_a(MN) = \log_a M + \log_a N, \quad \log_a\left(\frac{M}{N}\right) = \log_a M - \log_a N, \quad \log_a(M^k) = k\log_a M, \quad \log_a b = \frac{\ln b}{\ln a}

formulas.name: Exponential & Logarithmic Monotonicity Rules
formulas.expression: a > 1: \; a^{f(x)} < a^{g(x)} \iff f(x) < g(x); \qquad 0 < a < 1: \; a^{f(x)} < a^{g(x)} \iff f(x) > g(x)

solution_steps: Step 1: Domain condition: x - 1 > 0 and x + 1 > 0 => x > 1.
Step 3: x^2 = 9 => x = 3 or x = -3. Reject x = -3 since x > 1. Solution: x = 3.

hints: Enforce x - 2 > 0 and reverse the inequality sign because the base 1/2 < 1.

solution_steps: Step 1: Write all domain restrictions (arguments of all log terms > 0) before manipulating the equation.
Step 2: Express all terms in a common base a and combine logarithms.
Step 3: Solve the resulting algebraic equation and filter roots against the domain.

common_misconceptions.text: Accepting negative extraneous roots in logarithmic equations because they make the combined product (x - 1)(x + 1) positive.
common_misconceptions.correction: Every original logarithm term in the given equation must have a positive argument; check solutions against the original domain.

common_misconceptions.text: Keeping the inequality sign unchanged when removing a logarithm or exponential with base 0 < a < 1.
common_misconceptions.correction: When 0 < a < 1, a^x and log_a(x) are strictly decreasing functions, so the inequality direction must be reversed.

subject: Mathematics
subtopic: Compound & Double-Angle Formulas, Law of Sines/Cosines & Trig Equations
text: MoEYS Grade 11 Mathematics Chapter 3: Trigonometric Functions, Identities and Equations (អនុគមន៍ត្រីកោណមាត្រ រូបមន្តបំប្លែង និងសមីការត្រីកោណមាត្រ). Covers addition formulas for sin(a +- b), cos(a +- b), tan(a +- b), double-angle formulas sin(2a) = 2sin(a)cos(a) and cos(2a) = cos^2(a) - sin^2(a) = 2cos^2(a) - 1 = 1 - 2sin^2(a), power-reduction, sum-to-product and product-to-sum identities, solving fundamental trigonometric equations (sin x = sin alpha, cos x = cos alpha, tan x = tan alpha), and triangle geometry via the Law of Sines a/sin A = b/sin B = c/sin C = 2R and Law of Cosines c^2 = a^2 + b^2 - 2ab cos C.

Solve elementary and quadratic trigonometric equations and express general solutions with + 2k*pi or + k*pi

concepts.title: Addition, Double-Angle & Power-Reduction Formulas (រូបមន្តត្រីកោណមាត្រគ្រឹះ)
concepts.summary: Transforming sin(a +- b), cos(a +- b), sin(2a), cos(2a), sin^2(a), and cos^2(a).
concepts.body: cos(a +- b) = cos a cos b -+ sin a sin b; sin(a +- b) = sin a cos b +- cos a sin b. Setting b = a gives sin(2a) = 2sin a cos a and cos(2a) = 2cos^2 a - 1 = 1 - 2sin^2 a, which rearranges to the power-reduction formulas cos^2 a = (1 + cos 2a)/2 and sin^2 a = (1 - cos 2a)/2.

concepts.title: Trigonometric Equations & Triangle Laws (សមីការត្រីកោណមាត្រ និងទ្រឹស្តីបទក្នុងត្រីកោណ)
concepts.summary: General solutions of sin x = sin alpha, cos x = cos alpha, and Law of Sines/Cosines.
concepts.body:
1. sin x = sin alpha <=> x = alpha + 2k*pi or x = pi - alpha + 2k*pi (k in Z).
2. cos x = cos alpha <=> x = +-alpha + 2k*pi (k in Z).
3. tan x = tan alpha <=> x = alpha + k*pi (k in Z).
4. In any triangle ABC: c^2 = a^2 + b^2 - 2ab cos C and a/sin A = b/sin B = c/sin C = 2R.

formulas.name: Double-Angle & Power-Reduction Identities
formulas.expression: \sin 2a = 2\sin a\cos a, \quad \cos 2a = 2\cos^2 a - 1 = 1 - 2\sin^2 a, \quad \cos^2 a = \frac{1 + \cos 2a}{2}, \quad \sin^2 a = \frac{1 - \cos 2a}{2}
formulas.conditions: Valid for all real angles a

formulas.name: Fundamental Trigonometric Equation Solutions
formulas.expression: \cos x = \cos\alpha \iff x = \pm\alpha + 2k\pi; \quad \sin x = \sin\alpha \iff x = \alpha + 2k\pi \text{ or } x = \pi - \alpha + 2k\pi

formulas.name: Law of Cosines, Law of Sines & Triangle Area
formulas.expression: c^2 = a^2 + b^2 - 2ab\cos C, \quad \frac{a}{\sin A} = \frac{b}{\sin B} = \frac{c}{\sin C} = 2R, \quad S = \frac{1}{2}ab\sin C

solution_steps: Step 1: Factor the quadratic in t = cos x: (2t + 1)(t - 1) = 0 => cos x = 1 or cos x = -1/2.
Step 2: On [0, 2pi], cos x = 1 gives x = 0 and x = 2pi.
Step 3: cos x = -1/2 = cos(2pi/3) gives x = 2pi/3 and x = 2pi - 2pi/3 = 4pi/3.

examples.problem: In triangle ABC, side a = 5, side b = 8, and included angle C = 60 degrees. Find side c and the area S of the triangle.

hints: Write 1/2 = sin(pi/6) and apply the two branches of sin u = sin alpha.
solution_steps: Branch 1: 2x - pi/6 = pi/6 + 2k*pi => 2x = pi/3 + 2k*pi => x = pi/6 + k*pi.
Branch 2: 2x - pi/6 = 5pi/6 + 2k*pi => 2x = pi + 2k*pi => x = pi/2 + k*pi.

hints: Use cos(alpha) = sqrt(1 - sin^2 alpha) and sin(2alpha) = 2 sin(alpha) cos(alpha).

solution_steps: Step 1: Use double-angle or Pythagorean identities to rewrite the equation in terms of a single trigonometric function.
Step 2: Solve for the trig ratio and verify it lies in [-1, 1] for sin/cos.
Step 3: Write both general solution branches and divide by the coefficient of x.

common_misconceptions.text: Writing only one branch x = alpha + 2k*pi for sin x = sin alpha and forgetting x = pi - alpha + 2k*pi.
common_misconceptions.correction: Because sin(pi - alpha) = sin(alpha), sine equations have two supplementary families of solutions on the unit circle.

common_misconceptions.text: Forgetting to divide the period +2k*pi by n when solving cos(nx) = cos(alpha).
common_misconceptions.correction: Dividing nx = +-alpha + 2k*pi by n yields x = +-alpha/n + 2k*pi/n.

metadata.khmer_description: សិក្សាប្រមាណវិធីបូក-ដក-គុណម៉ាទ្រីស ដេទែមីណង់លំដាប់២ និងលំដាប់៣ ម៉ាទ្រីសច្រាស A^{-1} និងការដោះស្រាយប្រព័ន្ធសមីការលីនេអ៊ែរតាមម៉ាទ្រីស និងវិធានក្រាមែរ (Cramer)។
learning_objectives: Perform matrix addition, scalar multiplication, and non-commutative matrix multiplication AB
Evaluate 2x2 and 3x3 determinants and determine when a square matrix is invertible (det A != 0)
Compute the inverse matrix A^{-1} and solve linear systems AX = B using X = A^{-1}B and Cramer's Rule

concepts.title: Matrix Multiplication & Determinants (ការគុណម៉ាទ្រីស និងដេទែមីណង់)
concepts.summary: Row-by-column product AB (generally AB != BA) and det(AB) = det(A)det(B).
concepts.body: If A is (m x n) and B is (n x p), their product C = AB is (m x p) with entry c_{ij} equal to the dot product of row i of A and column j of B. For a 2x2 matrix [[a, b], [c, d]], det(A) = ad - bc.

concepts.title: Inverse Matrix & Cramer's Rule (ម៉ាទ្រីសច្រាស និងវិធានក្រាមែរ)
concepts.summary: Computing A^{-1} when det(A) != 0 and solving AX = B.
concepts.body: A square matrix A is invertible iff det(A) != 0. For 2x2 matrix A = [[a, b], [c, d]], A^{-1} = (1/(ad - bc)) [[d, -b], [-c, a]]. For linear system AX = B with D = det(A) != 0, X = A^{-1}B, or by Cramer's rule x = D_x/D, y = D_y/D.

formulas.name: 2x2 Determinant & Inverse Matrix
formulas.expression: A = \begin{pmatrix} a & b \\ c & d \end{pmatrix} \implies \det(A) = ad - bc, \quad A^{-1} = \frac{1}{ad - bc}\begin{pmatrix} d & -b \\ -c & a \end{pmatrix}

formulas.name: Cramer's Rule for Linear Systems
formulas.expression: AX = B \iff X = A^{-1}B, \quad x = \frac{D_x}{D}, \quad y = \frac{D_y}{D}, \quad z = \frac{D_z}{D} \quad (D = \det A \neq 0)

variables.D_x, D_y, D_z: Determinants with column replaced by B

examples.problem: Given A = \begin{pmatrix} 2 & 1 \\ 5 & 3 \end{pmatrix}, find \det(A) and A^{-1}, then solve \begin{cases} 2x + y = 4 \\ 5x + 3y = 11 \end{cases}.
solution_steps: Step 2: Swap main diagonal and negate off-diagonal: A^{-1} = [[3, -1], [-5, 2]].
Step 1: Expand along the first row: D = 1*(3*2 - 1*1) - 2*(0*2 - 1*2) + 0.

exercises.prompt: Find all values of m for which A = \begin{pmatrix} m & 2 \\ 8 & m \end{pmatrix} is singular (non-invertible).
Compute AB for A = \begin{pmatrix} 1 & 2 \\ 0 & 3 \end{pmatrix} and B = \begin{pmatrix} 2 & -1 \\ 1 & 4 \end{pmatrix}.
hints: Multiply rows of A by columns of B.

solution_steps: Step 1: Check matrix dimensions before multiplying (inner dimensions must match).
Step 2: Compute det(A) first; if det(A) = 0, A^{-1} does not exist.
Step 3: Check A * A^{-1} = I to verify the inverse matrix.

common_misconceptions.text: Assuming matrix multiplication is commutative (AB = BA) or that (A + B)^2 = A^2 + 2AB + B^2.
common_misconceptions.correction: Matrix multiplication is generally not commutative (AB != BA), so (A + B)^2 = A^2 + AB + BA + B^2.

common_misconceptions.text: Multiplying two matrices element-by-element (entrywise) instead of row-by-column.
common_misconceptions.correction: Entry (i, j) of AB is the dot product of row i of A with column j of B.

subject: Mathematics
subtopic: Newton's Binomial Theorem, General Term & Descriptive Statistics
text: MoEYS Grade 11 Mathematics Chapters 5 & 6: Combinatorics, Newton's Binomial Theorem, and Statistics (ចម្លាស់ បន្សំ ទ្វេធាញូតុន និងស្ថិតិ). Newton's Binomial Theorem expands (a + b)^n = sum_{k=0}^n C(n, k) a^{n-k} b^k, where the (k + 1)-th general term is T_{k+1} = C(n, k) a^{n-k} b^k and Pascal's identity is C(n, k) + C(n, k+1) = C(n+1, k+1). In descriptive statistics, a frequency distribution (x_i, n_i) with total N = sum n_i has mean x_bar = (1/N) sum n_i x_i, variance s^2 = (1/N) sum n_i (x_i - x_bar)^2 = (1/N) sum n_i x_i^2 - x_bar^2, and standard deviation s = sqrt(s^2).

metadata.starter_problem: \text{Find the coefficient of } x^3 \text{ in the expansion of } (2x - 1)^5
learning_objectives: Expand (a + b)^n using Newton's Binomial Theorem and Pascal's Triangle
Find a specific power term or constant term using the general term T_{k+1} = C(n, k) a^{n-k} b^k
Calculate mean, median, variance, and standard deviation of grouped and ungrouped statistical data

concepts.title: Newton's Binomial Expansion (រូបមន្តទ្វេធាញូតុន)
concepts.summary: Expansion of (a + b)^n into (n + 1) terms and finding targeted powers of x.
concepts.body: The expansion of (a + b)^n has (n + 1) terms with general term T_{k+1} = C(n, k) a^{n-k} b^k (0 <= k <= n). Setting a = b = 1 proves that the sum of all binomial coefficients is C(n, 0) + C(n, 1) + ... + C(n, n) = 2^n.

concepts.title: Measures of Central Tendency & Dispersion (មធ្យម វ៉ារ្យង់ និងគម្លាតស្តង់ដា)
concepts.summary: Quantifying center (mean, median) and spread (variance, standard deviation).
concepts.body: For data values x_i with frequencies n_i (sum n_i = N), the mean is x_bar = (sum n_i x_i)/N, the variance is V = (sum n_i x_i^2)/N - x_bar^2, and the standard deviation is sigma = sqrt(V).

examples.problem: Find the coefficient of x^3 in the expansion of (2x - 1)^5.
solution_steps: Step 1: Write the general term: T_{k+1} = C(5, k) (2x)^{5-k} (-1)^k = C(5, k) 2^{5-k} (-1)^k x^{5-k}.
Step 2: Match the exponent of x^3: 5 - k = 3 => k = 2.
Step 3: Coefficient is C(5, 2) * 2^3 * (-1)^2 = 10 * 8 * 1 = 80. Wait: for x^3, 5-k=3 => k=2, so (-1)^2 = +1 => +80; for x^2 (k=3) it is -80. Thus for x^3 (k=2), coefficient is +80.

examples.problem: Find the mean and variance of the dataset: 2, 4, 6, 8, 10.

exercises.prompt: Find the constant term (independent of x) in the expansion of \left(x + \frac{2}{x}\right)^4.

solution_steps: Step 1: Write the general term T_{k+1} = C(n, k) a^{n-k} b^k and collect all x factors into a single power x^{p(k)}.
Step 2: Set p(k) equal to the desired exponent (0 for the constant term) and solve for k.
Step 3: Substitute k back into the numerical coefficient.

common_misconceptions.text: Dropping the negative sign of b when expanding (a - b)^n.
common_misconceptions.correction: Write (a - b)^n = (a + (-b))^n so the factor (-1)^k alternates signs correctly.

common_misconceptions.text: Forgetting to subtract x_bar^2 in the computational variance formula (1/N) sum n_i x_i^2 - x_bar^2.
common_misconceptions.correction: Variance is the mean of the squares minus the square of the mean: E(X^2) - [E(X)]^2.
